issues.description: Resource IDs are interpolated directly into URL paths, allowing slashes or query characters to change the requested endpoint.
batch_create materializes the entire iterable before chunking, breaking the documented any-size iterable behavior and risking large memory spikes.
Pagination has no guard for repeated cursors, so a bad API response can create an infinite loop.
Malformed successful responses leak KeyError/TypeError/ValueError from model parsing instead of raising a typed LumenAPIError.
Non-object items in API result arrays are silently skipped, causing data loss instead of surfacing schema corruption.
Retry-After only supports numeric seconds and ignores valid HTTP-date values.
Retry sleeps are uncapped, so a malicious or broken Retry-After header can block the process for an arbitrary duration.
max_attempts is not validated, allowing zero or negative values that skip the request and return a misleading error.
Custom base_url values are accepted without requiring HTTPS, making it easy to send API keys over plaintext by mistake.
Boolean fields use bool(...) coercion, so values like "false" are interpreted as true.
Literal-constrained fields are not runtime-validated, allowing impossible statuses or verdicts into typed model objects.
Public type aliases used by the client API are not exported, reducing usability for typed consumers.
